analysis: All units are documentation-only; I found no concrete security regression. docs/reference/configuration.md (~148-157) now documents a default concurrency of 8 on M5 Pro/Max/Ultra for models on the native `auto` paged allowlist. It falls back to 4 under Low Power Mode or thermal pressure. A stamped 4 and explicit per-model caps are not raised. This is an availability and memory-admission description (T-029, T-010 adjacent). It adds no new trust boundary, and the doc says architecture and physical memory limits still apply. The code that implements it (ServingPerformanceProfiles.automaticConcurrency, EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.preferredBackend) was not supplied, so it was not checked. Wider concurrency on a shared engine could slightly change the T-041 prefix-cache TTFT oracle and the KV memory pressure. This is not demonstrated and falls under the existing accepted SEC-035 risk. docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head text only, no diff hunks shown) was reviewed for consistency with the threat model. It describes the cache's default-on status, the SSD TTL and disk budget, and the forwarding of cache environment variables to the LaunchAgent. It also describes the App Attest worker opt-in (`DARKBLOOM_APP_ATTEST_WORKER_QUALIFICATION`, forwarded only when exactly `1`, matching the TB-011 default-off candidate), fan helper paths, and the report command's evidence redaction. All of this matches the threat model, and I found nothing contradictory. Line 1503 has a malformed table row: the `memory_reserve_gb` key cell is unterminated. That is a cosmetic docs bug and not security-relevant. Since the cli-reference changes could not be isolated from unchanged text, a later pass should check whether code changes accompany these docs. Specifically, it should confirm that the M5 concurrency default does not bypass memory-admission checks.
